body.en:
Question B-008-003-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Parasitic oscillations are not limited to harmonics or the fundamental; an RF amplifier can oscillate unintentionally above or below the intended transmit frequency.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "on VHF frequencies only": Parasitics can occur outside VHF; the mechanism depends on circuit feedback and layout, not only on one frequency region.
- sourceIndex 2: "on the transmitter fundamental frequency": The transmitter fundamental frequency is the intended signal, whereas a parasitic is an additional unwanted oscillation.
- sourceIndex 3: "on harmonics of the transmitter frequency": Harmonics are exact multiples of the transmitter frequency; parasitic oscillations need not fall on those multiples.
